dedupe_keys.name: national disaster preparedness baseline assessment of suriname pacific disaster center 2024

description: The National Disaster Preparedness Baseline Assessment of Suriname is a 148-page report published in 2024 by the Pacific Disaster Center, prepared with Suriname's national disaster coordination centre (NCCR) and many ministries and agencies. It has two parts. The Risk and Vulnerability Assessment looks at multi-hazard exposure, socio-economic vulnerability and coping capacity across the districts, and the Disaster Management Analysis takes a qualitative look at six subthemes, from the enabling environment and institutional arrangements to disaster governance. The summary says that extreme heat, riverine and coastal flooding, mosquito-borne disease and earthquake give considerable exposure of people, buildings and critical infrastructure, that access to energy and technology and public health capacity limit coping capacity, and that the absence of an approved disaster management law hinders NCCR. It lists recommendations such as a planning audit and resilient agricultural infrastructure. The report says its data and results are available in PDC's DisasterAWARE Pro application. Access to the report is free as a PDF; no licence is stated, and DisasterAWARE Pro needs an account. Caveats: the district indices are shown in the report as maps and tables, not as downloadable data. Coverage is Suriname. It supports multi-hazard exposure and vulnerability analysis; related records are the INFORM Risk Index and ThinkHazard.
